title: M. Abul Kalam Azad | Senior Economist, World Bank
gist: A World Bank staff-profile page for Senior Economist Mohammad Abul Azad, whose research spans conflict/displacement data and whose 2026 post history shows a pivot toward agriculture resilience in Nigeria and Liberia and the biofuels-agriculture-energy security nexus.

themes.theme: 2026 Research Pivot to Agriculture and Energy Security

insights.claim: Azad's most recent posts (2026) center on agricultural resilience in Nigeria ('From loss to resilience in Nigeria: turning a growing agricultural challenge into action,' July 2026), a new agriculture census and survey in Liberia (June 2026), and biofuels/oil insecurity's link to agriculture-powered mobility (April 2026) — a cluster of posts suggesting a World Bank Development Data Group research push into the agriculture-energy security nexus in West Africa during 2026.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Signals a live World Bank data/research thread on West African agriculture and energy security worth monitoring for new datasets (e.g., the new Liberia agriculture census) and policy recommendations.
insights.locator: From loss to resilience in Nigeria: turning a growing agricultural challenge into action, July 22, 2026

themes.theme: Background in Conflict and Displacement Data

insights.claim: Azad has over twenty-five years of experience in fragile, conflict, and violence (FCV) settings, where he contributed to closing evidence gaps on forcibly displaced populations and developed conflict monitoring systems used to inform recovery and reconstruction policy.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Positions Azad's institutional expertise as a bridge between conflict-monitoring data infrastructure and agricultural/food-security analysis — relevant for understanding how World Bank FCV data tools feed into broader development lending.
insights.locator: He has extensive experience in fragile, conflict, and violence (FCV) settings
